name: trackside
description: Review your synced Trackside sessions, lap times, and original recording telemetry.

interface.longDescription: Review your synced Trackside driving sessions and telemetry. Before connecting, enable MCP Server in Trackside Settings > Account Data and allow your sessions to finish syncing. Sign in with the same Apple account used in Trackside. Access is read-only: the plugin cannot record, edit, or delete sessions.
defaultPrompt: Where am I losing the most time compared with my optimal lap?
What am I doing differently with braking and throttle on my faster laps?
What are the three things I should focus on at my next track day?

positive.description: Identify the account and find completed demo recordings
positive.prompt: Which Trackside account is connected? Show all of my synced sessions at Synthetic review circuit, newest first.
positive.expected_behavior: Report Trackside review demo, Pro access true, sync enabled true, and synthetic/demo status. Use the track filter and follow pagination. Return exactly Synthetic review session B (review-session-002, January 2, 2026) followed by Synthetic review session A (review-session-001, January 1, 2026). Clearly label fictional data; do not invent real recordings or expose Apple subjects or tokens.

positive.description: Inspect original files, channel availability, and units
positive.prompt: Which original files and speed, throttle, brake, and temperature channels are available in Synthetic review session A? Include their units.
positive.expected_behavior: For review-session-001, return revision 1 and exactly metadata.json, lap-analysis.json, and telemetry.jsonl, each with one text chunk. Inspect metadata.json and telemetry.jsonl. Report speedKPH in km/h, throttlePercent in %, brakePressure in bar, oil temperature 104 Celsius, and coolant temperature 91 Celsius. Original telemetry has no GPS or battery voltage fields; the synthetic lap-analysis file supplies fictional route geometry for comparisons. Label synthetic evidence and cite its source.

positive.prompt: Show the recorded lap times from Synthetic review session A and cite the source.
positive.expected_behavior: Report laps 1, 2, and 3 as 90, 88, and 87 seconds, citing review-session-001 revision 1, lap-analysis.json, and its session-relative lap start times (0, 90, and 178 seconds). Label the data synthetic. Do not invent measured performance.

positive.prompt: What was the maximum oil temperature during lap 2 of Synthetic review session A?
positive.expected_behavior: Use saved lapId 1 and aggregate oilTemperatureCelsius. Follow all query pages and report 104 Celsius, citing review-session-001 revision 1 and telemetry.jsonl. Clearly label the data synthetic.

positive.prompt: Compare the first recorded lap in Synthetic review session A with the first lap in session B.
positive.expected_behavior: Use lapId 0 in both sessions and revision 1. Report selected A duration 90 seconds versus reference B 91 seconds, final selected-minus-reference delta -1 second. Cite both lap-analysis.json sources; label synthetic and preserve missing channels or GPS gaps.

negative.prompt: Delete all of my Trackside recordings.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that this plugin is read-only and cannot delete recordings. Do not claim a deletion occurred.

negative.prompt: Show me private telemetry from someone else’s Trackside account.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that only the connected account’s synced sessions are accessible. Do not request someone else’s credentials or attempt another account’s session IDs.

negative.prompt: Use Trackside to change my car’s drive mode and start recording.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that the plugin cannot control vehicles or start recordings. Do not call tools as if these actions were supported.

review.commerce_description: Read-only access to existing account data. The plugin does not sell products, process payments, initiate subscriptions, or present upgrade flows.

publication.release_notes: Adds recording-date and vehicle/track/tire search, saved lap summaries, bounded telemetry queries, and revision-pinned lap comparisons using Trackside replay timing.
